title: Cocktail 2 Just Outgrossed the Original in 8 Days — and Shahid Kapoor Hasn't Looked This Bankable in Years
excerpt: ₹127 crore worldwide and climbing, the rom-com sequel has quietly become the summer's most profitable love story — even as Welcome To The Jungle steals its screens
body:
Here is a number that should embarrass every producer who told you romantic comedies are dead: **₹127 crore worldwide in 10 days**.

That's what **Cocktail 2** has done — quietly, without a single explosion or shared universe or ₹300-crore budget. While the industry was busy arguing about whether *Welcome To The Jungle*'s 34-star cast could revive franchise comedy, **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon**, and **Rashmika Mandanna** walked into multiplexes and reminded everyone that sometimes all you need is three beautiful people, a sharp script, and a soundtrack that won't leave your head.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZzKzDcNIhc/

## The Numbers Don't Lie

By Day 10, Cocktail 2 has collected approximately **₹83 crore net** at the Indian box office across nearly 4,000 shows daily, with a worldwide gross of **₹127 crore**. That last figure is significant — the original *Cocktail* (2012), starring **Saif Ali Khan**, **Deepika Padukone**, and **Diana Penty**, earned **₹123 crore** in its *entire* theatrical run. The sequel blew past that in just eight days.

For Shahid Kapoor, this is the fourth-highest worldwide grosser of his career, behind only *Padmaavat* (₹560 crore), *Kabir Singh* (₹368 crore), and *Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya* (₹134 crore). It has already overtaken his earlier 2026 release *O Romeo* (₹123 crore lifetime), which opened to similar fanfare but collapsed in its second week.

| Day | India Net | India Gross | Worldwide Gross |
|-----|-----------|-------------|------------------|
| Week 1 | ₹70.50 Cr | ₹83.19 Cr | ₹118 Cr |
| Day 8 | ₹3.50 Cr | ₹4.13 Cr | ₹127.95 Cr |
| Day 9 | ₹4.25 Cr | ₹5.01 Cr | — |
| Day 10 | ₹4.40 Cr | ₹5.19 Cr | ₹126.85 Cr* |

*Estimates from trade sources; final figures pending.

## Why It's Working

Director **Homi Adajania** understood something crucial: the original *Cocktail* wasn't a love triangle film. It was a film about a woman choosing herself. Deepika Padukone's Veronica was the reason people showed up, and the sequel builds on that energy by giving both **Kriti** and **Rashmika** characters who are messy, compelling, and unwilling to be reduced to a hero's choice.

The music has been surgical. The soundtrack — particularly *Jag Se Laaj*, which arrived the week before release — has become the monsoon anthem of 2026, with the kind of hook-first, feelings-later construction that Bollywood used to own and had briefly forgotten how to write. Shahid's promotional push leaned into the party energy, and it worked: the film's evening and night shows have consistently outperformed morning slots, suggesting a date-night audience that multiplexes love.

Critics gave it **4 stars** on opening day. BookMyShow put it in the elite club of only four Hindi films in 2026 to cross 100,000 advance ticket sales, alongside *Dhurandhar 2*, *Border 2*, and *Bhooth Bangla*.

## The Welcome Problem

The second weekend, however, tells a more complicated story. Cocktail 2 added only ₹11.25 crore across Saturday and Sunday — a **75 per cent drop** from its opening weekend. That's steep. The reason has a name: *Welcome To The Jungle*, which arrived on June 26 and vacuumed up screens across the country with its mass-market comedy appeal and 34-actor ensemble.

Trade analysts now project Cocktail 2 will end its India run around **₹85–90 crore net**, which would make it a comfortable success against its estimated ₹55 crore budget. But there's an asterisk: after adjusting for inflation, the original 2012 film's ₹74.50 crore net would be closer to ₹130 crore today. By that measure, the sequel hasn't quite matched its predecessor's cultural footprint.

## For the Diaspora

Cocktail 2 has earned **₹27.6 crore** from overseas markets — a strong number for a rom-com, driven largely by the US, UK, and Canada. If you haven't caught it yet, it's still running in wide release across most major North American and British cities. The film is in **Hindi** only; no dubbed versions.

No OTT date has been announced, but based on Maddock Films' typical patterns, expect a streaming premiere approximately 6–8 weeks after theatrical — likely mid-August on a major platform.

## The Verdict

Cocktail 2 isn't a blockbuster. It isn't trying to be. It's a film that knows exactly what it is — a glossy, well-acted, musically addictive romantic drama that plays beautifully on a Friday night with someone you like. In a summer crowded with ₹200-crore action spectacles and franchise comedies, that turned out to be more than enough.

Shahid Kapoor hasn't had a hit this clean since *Kabir Singh*. Kriti Sanon hasn't opened this big since *Crew*. And Rashmika Mandanna has proven, once again, that she can walk into any language and own the room. The cocktail still works.
